problem.title: What does your team actually do all day?

items.title: Retyping the same data
items.desc: One shipment's data gets retyped four or five times — quotation, S/O, B/L, customs declaration. Same cargo description, same counts, same marks.

items.title: Quotes go out too slow
items.desc: Chase rates, wait for replies, stitch the Excel together — half a day later, the buyer already booked with whoever quoted first.

items.title: Can't hire for the desk
items.desc: The docs-clerk opening has been up for three months. Whoever comes needs six months of training — then leaves.

problem.punchLead: And it's not just your company —
problem.punchEmph: Taiwan's job boards carry thousands of unfilled docs-clerk openings, permanently.

howItWorks.subtitle: Keep your systems and your habits. AI drafts, people check the exceptions.

whyUs.title: AI reads. Deterministic code does the math.
whyUs.para1Title: Semantics go to AI; every calculation is deterministic.
whyUs.para1: Reading a messy inquiry email or judging which documents a shipment needs — that's for large language models. But every calculation and field mapping runs through verifiable program logic: every number can answer "why is it this number."
whyUs.para2Title: Built for how Taiwan actually works.
whyUs.para2: Taiwan's document formats, the customs ecosystem, inboxes that mix Chinese and English — the things overseas tools can't read, we do. Meriq is built with a customs brokerage team with 43 years of experience; their judgment is written into every check rule.

faq.title: What owners and OPs ask us

items.a: You can start within a week. Nothing in your current setup moves — forward inquiry emails and documents as-is and it runs. No data migration, no workflow changes.

items.q: What if the AI gets customs data wrong?
items.a: Every calculation and field mapping runs through deterministic code, so every number is traceable. Anything the AI isn't sure about is flagged, and the OP confirms before anything is sent. It's also worth asking the other way: what's the error rate of retyping the same data four or five times by hand today? Meriq's check report exists to catch exactly those errors before they go out.
Encrypted in transit and at rest, tenant-isolated per company, and we never train models on your customer data.
No. Meriq removes the retyping and copy-pasting they hate most — not the job. OPs become the people who judge exceptions and make calls. That's the skill worth paying for; retyping isn't.

items.q: How is this different from the systems out there?
items.a: Systems solve where data is stored. Meriq solves how data gets in — the manual stretch between an inquiry email or a document and structured data is where the day actually goes. That's why Meriq replaces nothing: its output imports straight into whatever system you already use.
